paper_title: Chiplet Multi-Objective Optimization Algorithm Based on Communication Consumption and Temperature

scenario.description: Multi-window display (MWD) system with 12 IP cores separated into 12 chiplets for 2.5-D integration using passive interposer. Communication task diagram shows data rates between chiplets. Chiplet sizes and power dissipation defined for thermal-aware mapping optimization.
scenario.architecture: 2.5-D passive interposer-based heterogeneous system with 12 chiplets, mesh network-on-chip topology, organic substrate (FR-4), C4 bumps, silicon interposer, microbumps, thermal interface material, spreader, and air-forced heatsink with forced convection cooling.
scenario.workload: Multi-window display multimedia application; communication tasks defined in Table 1 with priorities and data rates (Mbit/s) ranging from 64 to 256 Mbit/s between chiplet pairs.
scenario.operating_point: Ambient temperature 318.5 K, heatsink edge size 20 mm, spreader edge size 5 mm, fin-channel heatsink with 30 mm fin-height and 1 mm fin-width, 10 cm fan radius at 5000 RPM, chiplet power values from Table 2 ranging 5–70 W (mem3: 10 W, hs: 40 W, nr: 70 W, in: 30 W, vs: 10 W, mem2: 10 W, hvs: 30 W, jug1: 20 W, jug2: 30 W, se: 50 W, mem1: 10 W, blend: 5 W).

original_setup.optimizer: Chiplet Multi-Objective Optimization (CMO) algorithm based on symmetry mapping
original_setup.controller: weight factor α (0 ≤ α ≤ 1) for balancing communication and temperature optimization
original_setup.benchmark: Multi-window display (MWD) system with 12 IP cores

physical_mismatches.reason: Hotspot uses compact thermal modeling based on stacked-layer packaging (RC circuit model with fourth-order Runge-Kutta solver) rather than true transient 3D finite element simulation; assumes uniform power distribution and consistent surface temperature across chiplets due to thinness and high thermal conductivity assumption [29]
Algorithm uses Manhattan distance in 2D mesh topology for inter-chiplet communication and thermal calculations, not 3D through-silicon via (TSV) thermal paths or actual interposer heat conduction

Air-forced heatsink with lateral airflow and fin-channel design specified but single convection coefficient applied; does not account for non-uniform flow distribution or local coolant temperature variations

Chiplet sizes preprocessed with spacing included as 'theoretical size' in topology (e.g., blend 4.0×4.0 mm theoretical vs 2.5×2.5 mm actual) but spacing implementation not explicitly detailed in power or thermal model

studio_assumptions: Power is evenly distributed over chiplet area
Surface temperature of each chiplet is consistent with overall chiplet temperature due to high thermal conductivity
Chiplet theoretical sizes include mandatory spacing; unit grid size derived from largest chiplet
Communication-based heuristic information proportional to Manhattan distance and communication data rate with fixed Ebit=0.186 energy per Mbit per unit distance
Temperature-based heuristic information inversely proportional to distance and proportional to already-mapped chiplet power (Equation 2)
Weight factor α=0.5 balances communication and temperature equally; α=0.8 prioritizes communication, α=0.2 prioritizes temperature
Ambient temperature held constant at 318.5 K
Heatsink specifications: 20 mm edge, 30 mm fin-height, 1 mm fin-width, 10 cm fan radius, 5000 RPM fan speed
Spreader edge size 5 mm, thermal interface material properties assumed in Hotspot default
Chiplets occupy discrete grid nodes; unmapped nodes represent available placement space
missing_inputs: Hotspot 7.0 configuration file (chiplet material properties, C4 bump dimensions, silicon interposer thickness, microbump specifications, TSV dimensions, TIM thermal properties)
Measured or simulated validation data for MWD system (no comparison to silicon measurements or other simulators)
Repository URL or supplementary data release (paper states 'data reported in this study are included in the article' but no external repository linked)
Exact chiplet layout coordinates for the CMO optimized solution (only thermal maps shown, numerical positions not provided)
Energy per bit specification Ebit value derivation or reference
Single-objective optimization benchmark [31] detailed parameters and results
Transient temperature profiles or time-to-steady-state specification
Power profile variations across chiplets during operation (constant power assumed)
